draft.title: The electromagnetic spectrum
card: The electromagnetic spectrum is the family of electromagnetic waves. In order of increasing frequency, it is radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma rays.
The waves differ only in wavelength and frequency. Higher frequency means shorter wavelength.
All of them travel at the same speed, c, in a vacuum. Here c = fλ, so if the frequency goes up, the wavelength must go down.
Gamma rays have the highest frequency and the shortest wavelength. Radio waves have the lowest frequency and the longest wavelength.
draft.remember: One family of waves: all travel at c in a vacuum, and only frequency and wavelength differ.

a.q: Which statement correctly compares X-rays with microwaves in a vacuum?
opts: X-rays have a higher frequency and the same speed
X-rays have a higher frequency and a higher speed
X-rays have a lower frequency and the same speed
X-rays have a shorter wavelength and a lower speed
a.why: X-rays are higher in frequency than microwaves, and so have a shorter wavelength. All electromagnetic waves travel at c in a vacuum, so the speed is the same. The tempting idea that higher frequency means faster is wrong, because c = fλ and the wavelength shortens to compensate.
a.clue: Does the speed in a vacuum change along the spectrum?

b.q: A radio wave and a beam of ultraviolet light travel through a vacuum. Which statement is correct?
opts: The radio wave has the longer wavelength
The radio wave has the higher frequency
The ultraviolet light reaches a target first
The ultraviolet light has the longer wavelength
b.why: Radio waves have a lower frequency than ultraviolet, so by c = fλ they have a longer wavelength. Both travel at c in a vacuum, so neither arrives first. Choosing the ultraviolet as faster confuses frequency with speed.
b.clue: Both waves travel at c, so compare frequency and wavelength only.

a.best: X-rays have a higher frequency and the same speed

b.best: The radio wave has the longer wavelength
